input.quote: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b).
input.rationale: Section 11.3 is the only right binding Customer that operates as an inspection/verification right: IBM may investigate suspected AUP violations without any frequency limit, without prior notice (notice is only "attempt[ed]" before restricting access or removing Content, and not for the investigation itself), and with no cost allocation, reinforced by Customer's open-ended obligation in p0138 to supply "all relevant information ... at IBM's request." Unlimited and unannounced verification is walk-away territory under AUDIT, so we redline to the fallback: once per year, 15 days' prior notice, and IBM bears costs unless underpayment exceeds 10%. We have not proposed the preferred independent-auditor, off-site or no-system-access terms, which remain available if IBM will not accept the fallback wording.

mappings.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.

proposal.summary: Add frequency, notice and cost limits to IBM's investigation/verification right in 11.3
proposal.comment: [Playbook] IBM's investigation right and the related information-request obligation are currently unlimited and unannounced. We add our fallback audit limits: once per year, 15 days' prior notice, and IBM bears the cost unless it establishes an underpayment exceeding 10%.

ops.text: IBM may exercise its investigation and verification rights under this Subsection 11.3 no more than once per year and only upon at least fifteen (15) days' prior notice to Customer, and IBM will bear all costs of each such investigation unless it establishes an underpayment by Customer exceeding ten percent (10%).
